preamble: The change of the voiceless velar stop [k] to the labiodental fricative or approximant [v] is a lenition in which the velar closure is weakened and the resulting segment takes on labial articulation, usually through an intermediate spirant stage [ɣ] or under the influence of rounded vowels. In Samic, Proto-Samic *k turned into *v before the sonorants *l, *j and *ń (earlier *keklä 'ring' > *keavlē > Northern Sami geavli), and in Finnish consonant gradation the weak grade of k between rounded vowels is v (puku : puvun).

examples.to: Proto-Samic *čivlē > Northern Sami čivhli, Inari Sami čivle
examples.note: Reconstructed stage: the clusters *kl, *kj and *kń became *vl, *vj and *vń in Proto-Samic; compare Proto-Finnic *süklä with retained k.
Reconstructed stage; the loanword was adopted with *kl and underwent the native *kl > *vl change.
Reconstructed stage; Lithuanian deglis 'tinder' and Latvian dagla preserve the Baltic source shape.
In the environment -uku- / -yky-, the weak grade of k is v.

sources: Sammallahti, P. (1998). The Saami Languages: An Introduction. Davvi Girji. https://lccn.loc.gov/00308815
